# Regulatory Landscape

This section maps the legal and normative frameworks that shape responsible AI for EO and states how each one applies. The guideline is aligned with the GDPR, the principles of the AI Act and the European Code of Conduct for Research Integrity, and work involving partners outside the EU should also meet the relevant regulations of their jurisdictions. Because regulations and standards keep evolving, they are tracked over time; the tracking and escalation arrangements are described in the governance section. The provision-by-provision mapping is held in the standards crosswalk annex, and the PROTEUS commitments, including those for its non-EU partners, are in Annex I.

## EU AI Act

The EU AI Act is the binding European regulation for AI systems and follows a risk-based approach. This subsection summarises the obligations that can apply to EO AI outputs, notably for general-purpose and foundation models (documentation, transparency, risk assessment and security) and for AI used in sensitive domains such as migration monitoring or civil protection. It describes how models and use cases are assessed against the Act's categories and which parts of this guideline (principles, risk register, metadata schema, compliance process) serve as evidence of conformity. Because the research and prototype status of the work affects which obligations apply, it also notes where official guidance is still developing and how changes are followed.

## ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42

ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42 is the joint ISO and IEC subcommittee that develops international standards for artificial intelligence, including terminology, AI management systems, risk management, trustworthiness, bias and data quality. This subsection identifies the SC 42 standards that are relevant to AI4EO and FM development and relates their concepts to the principles of this guideline, so that the terminology and evaluation criteria remain compatible with international practice. The mapping is intended to feed the standards crosswalk table planned as an annex to this guideline.

## IEEE P7000

The IEEE P7000 series addresses ethical considerations in the design of autonomous and intelligent systems, with individual standards on topics such as ethical system design, transparency, data privacy and algorithmic bias. This guideline draws on the series, together with IEEE's Ethically Aligned Design, as a source of design-time practices. This subsection lists the parts of the series that inform the principles on transparency, fairness, privacy and social impact, and notes the IEEE GRSS community as a route for contributing to standards work in AI4EO.

## ITU-T

ITU-T recommendations and the related ITU work on AI give technical guidance on the use of AI for environmental monitoring and disaster management, on the environmental efficiency of AI, and on interoperability. This subsection records the relevant recommendations and indicates how they relate to requirements for EO services such as interoperability, quality and trust in AI-generated information.

## GDPR

The General Data Protection Regulation governs the processing of personal data and applies wherever data can relate to identifiable persons. EO AI work should use non-personal or anonymised data where possible, apply privacy, security and data minimisation, and store data in line with FAIR and INSPIRE standards. This subsection describes the GDPR touchpoints: lawful basis and consent where applicable, anonymisation and re-identification risk for high-resolution EO and in-situ data, licensing and intellectual property, and cross-border transfers involving partners outside the EU. It is coordinated with the applicable data management plan.
